subject: Break-Glass canary fallback & version-lock — SLA carveout request
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@nimblepay.com>, ops@nimblepay.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: Break-Glass canary fallback & version-lock — SLA carveout request

Elena / NimblePay ops team,

Following our pilot kickoff, NimblePay asked for stronger uptime guarantees on checkout paths while we validate the new opti-lm model. To avoid customer-facing degradations during canary/A-B experiments, we propose a temporary "break-glass" rule that allows automatic fallback and a short sticky version-lock under a narrowly-scoped SLA carveout. High-level proposal (details attached):

- Trigger: auto-fallback to a pinned stable variant when production telemetry crosses pre-defined thresholds (see matrix).
- Threshold examples: sustained p95 latency increase +25% vs baseline for 10 minutes OR sudden error-rate spike to >1.5% for 5 minutes.
- Action: immediate traffic switch to pinned version and enforce sticky pin for a short window to let caches / KV stores stabilise (suggest 30 minutes).
- Telemetry & audit: Redwood provides full request/response telemetry, roll-forward history, and a post-incident archive for 90 days.
- Scope & duration: carveout applies only to NimblePay checkout endpoints in us-east; pilot period = 60 days, then reevaluate.

Attached: nimble_slo_request.pdf and deployment_matrix.xlsx with proposed thresholds and rollback actions.

Requesting NimblePay sign-off + any required legal language so sales can publish the carveout as an amendment to the SOW. If you want a different sticky window or threshold, flag it and we can adjust.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

---

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-06-10T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Break-Glass canary fallback & version-lock — SLA carveout request

Jonas / Elena,

Thanks for the clear ask. From an engineering perspective I want to make two clarifications and propose concrete guardrails we can implement immediately: 

1) Thresholds and hysteresis: we should use relative deltas plus absolute floors to avoid noisy triggers. Proposed primary triggers:
   - p95 latency relative increase >= 25% AND absolute p95 > 400ms sustained for >= 10 minutes.
   - request error-rate (5xx + inference-timeouts) > 1.5% sustained for >= 5 minutes.
   - abrupt token-generation errors (e.g., model OOMs or KV cache misses) with >3x baseline should be considered emergency.

2) Sticky window and cooldown: automatic pin to stable variant for 30 minutes, with a 60-minute cooldown before automated un-pin attempts. During pinned state we will continue to run telemetry and attempt a canary every 15 mins (safety canary) that only resumes traffic if metrics look green for two consecutive canaries.

Operational notes:
- We will provide an immutable incident record for every fallback event (timestamp, reason, telemetry snapshot, triggering rule).
- Ops can opt for manual override if NimblePay requests immediate roll-forward.

Action items for NimblePay to sign off: acceptance of thresholds above OR provide alternative numbers; confirmation you accept the 30-minute sticky window or request different duration.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Engineering Manager, Runtime Reliability
Redwood Inference

Thanks — this looks reasonable and appreciated. A few small asks from NimblePay ops/legal: 

- Increase the sticky pin window to 60 minutes for checkout flows to reduce flip-flopping during high-traffic windows.
- We want the fallback telemetry exported daily to our S3 bucket (ops@nimblepay.com will share credentials via secure transfer).
- For contract amendment: please send a brief addendum we can sign (DocuSign) that states the carveout scope, thresholds, retention, and the pilot period.

Assuming those three items are included, NimblePay approves the approach and the pilot. Please include an explicit incident credit clause in the amendment if the fallback is triggered more than 3 times in a 30-day window.

Elena
